gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the per-metre term in a handheld scanner's volumetric-accuracy spec is multiplied by the length of the object being scanned (Revopoint: 'L is the length of the object'). For a reverse-engineering part, the error to expect is therefore base + rate × part length: about 0.06 mm for MetroX vs 0.032 mm for MetroX Pro on a 300 mm part. Creaform measures its figure as sphere spacing on a calibrated length artefact; Revopoint gives no test conditions.
standout_why: I compared against TriMech's SHINING 3D buyer's guide (cited), 3dscannermatch's reverse-engineering page (cited) and our own dealectric page. TriMech defines volumetric accuracy only as 'accuracy over longer distances' and gives no numbers or scaling. 3dscannermatch has no volumetric figures and does not mention VDI/VDE 2634. Our page lists the 'a + b mm/m' figures but never says what L is and never does the arithmetic. ChatGPT's own answer quoted the Rigil's '0.04 mm + 0.06 mm/m' and said to prefer 'verified volumetric accuracy', so the rivals have part of this. What none of them gives is the scaling by part length, the worked error for a given part size, or the fact that Creaform states its test method and Revopoint does not. The Creaform page cited in the chats (handyscan-3d-pro-series) returned 404 when I opened it, so I could not check what it says.
decides: This lets the page turn the shopper's tolerance into a pick. With the claimed specs, a part up to about 300 mm can be held near ±0.03-0.04 mm by MetroX Pro (0.032 mm) or HandySCAN 3D PRO (0.038 mm). Standard MetroX at its originally published spec reaches 0.06 mm, which is fine for '±0.1 mm mechanical fit' but not '±0.05 mm precision'. At 1 m the gap widens: MetroX 0.13 mm, MetroX Pro 0.06 mm, HandySCAN PRO 0.08 mm, HandySCAN PRO with MaxSHOT 0.045 mm. On paper this favours MetroX Pro over standard MetroX for anyone at or below ±0.05 mm. It also tells larger-part buyers to add photogrammetry (MaxSHOT or Revopoint's Global Marker mode). One caution: only Creaform states how its figure is measured (sphere spacing on a calibrated length artefact). Revopoint's figure has no stated test method, so the two sets of numbers are not measured the same way.
